title: Sliding Window Maximum
description:
Given an integer array nums and a width k, report the largest value in each consecutive subarray of exactly k elements, moving the window one position at a time from left to right. Return the maxima in window-start order. For an empty array, k is 0 and the result is []; otherwise k is between 1 and the array length.

Maintain indices of candidates in a deque, ordered so their values decrease from front to back. When a new value arrives, discard older candidates no greater than it: the new value survives at least as long and is never a worse maximum. Remove a front index once it exits the window. Each index enters and leaves at most once, so no window needs to be rescanned from scratch.

Equal maxima should yield their value once for each window, not a distinct index. Negative numbers count normally: the largest of [-5,-2] is -2. If k equals 1, the output matches nums; if k equals the entire nonempty array length, the output has one element.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [1,3,-1,-3,5,3,6,7], k = 3
Output: [3,3,5,5,6,7]

Example 2:

Input: nums = [4,-2,4], k = 2
Output: [4,4]

Example 3:

Input: nums = [], k = 0
Output: []

Constraints:

  • 0 <= nums.length <= 100,000
  • -1,000,000 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000
  • For nonempty nums, 1 <= k <= nums.length; for empty nums, k = 0.

exampleTestCases.explanation: Each value is the maximum of its three-element window.
